article_title: Cognition Launches Devin Bots and a McKinsey Alliance to Scale AI Coding as McKinsey Survey Finds 30% of Firms Saw Productivity Fall
summary: Automated checks passed; manual review found two instances where a cited outlet's own unquoted paraphrase was rendered as a direct quotation, and a missing Anthropic-maker disclosure sentence. Both quote issues and the disclosure gap are recoverable with corrections records; the headline, summary, and lead are fully supported by the cited sources.

findings.message: Body quotes "frontier-level performance for 60% less" as if it were Cognition's own words, but The Next Web (source-1) does not place this phrase in quotation marks.
findings.details: source-1.html.gz reads: "Cognition says Devin works with several AI models and matches each one to a different kind of work. It says this gives companies frontier-level performance for 60% less." This is The Next Web's own paraphrase of what Cognition says, not a quoted statement. The submission's Implications/Current-situation paragraph renders it as a direct quotation: 'Cognition says Devin's multi-model approach gives companies "frontier-level performance for 60% less,"'. The underlying 60%-less claim is accurately sourced; only the quotation marks are unsupported.

findings.message: Body quotes "even ship code" as if it were a verbatim fragment from SiliconANGLE, but the source does not quote it.
findings.details: source-2.html.gz reads: "Karan Ahuja, who leads the team, works with it to schedule user interviews and even ship code." This is SiliconANGLE's own narration describing Ahuja's usage, not a quotation from Ahuja or Anthropic. The submission's Background paragraph renders it as a direct quote: 'Karan Ahuja, who leads the Duet team, uses it to schedule interviews and "even ship code."' The underlying fact (Ahuja uses Duet to schedule interviews and ship code) is accurately sourced; only the quotation marks on "even ship code" are unsupported.

findings.message: Article names Anthropic in the lead and gives Claude Duet a dedicated background paragraph plus analysis-section comparison, but omits the required one-sentence disclosure that the Herald's contributor model is built by Anthropic.
findings.details: Per config/editorial_policy.md "Disclosure of the contributor model's maker": the policy's headline/summary/lead trigger is qualified by an exemption for "an incidental name in a list of vendors, benchmarks or competing models," which could cover the Overview's single comparative mention ("positioning the product against Anthropic's Duet and OpenAI's Dots"). However, the Background section goes well beyond that: it devotes a full paragraph to Claude Duet's October 22 launch, quotes SiliconANGLE on its framework and the Karan Ahuja usage detail, and the Implications section separately compares Duet's automatic-classifier security model to Devin Bots'. This is substantive treatment of an Anthropic product in passages of their own, not an incidental list mention, and the article contains no disclosure sentence anywhere.

content_preview.title: Cognition Launches Devin Bots and a McKinsey Alliance to Scale AI Coding as McKinsey Survey Finds 30% of Firms Saw Productivity Fall
content_preview.summary: Cognition paired a Devin Bots launch with a McKinsey alliance this week; McKinsey's own survey of 334 leaders found productivity fell at 30% of firms even as it more than doubled at the top quarter.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Cognition, the maker of the AI coding agent Devin, moved on two fronts within 48 hours in mid-November 2026. On November 16, it announced an alliance with McKinsey & Company to sell AI software engineering to large companies in the US and Europe, according to [The Next Web](https://thenextweb.com/news/cognition-mckinsey-alliance-devin-ai-software-engineering). The next day, it introduced Devin Bots, a tool that manages teams of Devin agents on projects spanning days or weeks, positi...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured Analysis with clearly separated Overview/Background/Current situation (facts) and Implications (analysis) sections. 1536 words, within the 800-2000 Analysis range. Neutral tone throughout; no sensationalism or AI self-reference.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 4 source snapshots were fetched successfully (HTTP 200, no archive fallback) and their sha256 hashes verified against manifest.json before reading. Read in full via gunzip + text extraction: source-0.html.gz (Fortune, 'Exclusive: Cognition bets on Devin Bots...', Nov 17 2026) confirms the Devin Bots description, Scott Wu quotes ('Self-driving software is...', the security-model quote, 'rather than relying on models themselves...'), the Interaction Company/Poke acquisition, the $1B ARR and $48B valuation figures, the tenfold Bots growth claim, and the Citigroup/Jane Fraser 14,000-engineer quote verbatim. source-1.html.gz (The Next Web, 'Cognition and McKinsey team up...', Nov 16 2026) confirms the McKinsey alliance terms, the Kaplan quote, the 334-leader/top-quarter-doubled/30%-fell survey figures, the Hämäläinen quote, the Levy/Ferrari quote (verbatim, confirmed via raw-text search), the six-of-eight-banks and three-of-six-insurers client figures, the Comarch ERP XL detail, and the Stamos/$48bn/$80bn financing timeline. It does NOT support the 'frontier-level performance for 60% less' phrase as a direct Cognition quote -- see findings. source-2.html.gz (SiliconANGLE, Claude Duet launch, Oct 22 2026) confirms Duet's description, availability (web/iOS/Android, Pro/Max), its basis in Anthropic's agent framework (Claude Code, Claude in Chrome), the automatic-classifier detail, and the Karan Ahuja usage detail -- but does NOT quote 'even ship code' verbatim; that phrase is SiliconANGLE's own narration. See findings. source-3.html.gz (TechCrunch, OpenAI Dots launch, Sept 29 2026) confirms the DevDay date, the 'remarkably capable, always-on agents built to handle everything' quote verbatim, the GPT-6 Astra basis, the Pro/Business Premium availability, deployment from Codex, and the customer-feedback-monitoring use case. No suspicious_patterns were flagged in manifest.json for any of the 4 sources; none required review as potential prompt injection. Independent-source count for the Analysis requirement: 4 of 4 sources (Fortune, The Next Web, SiliconANGLE, TechCrunch) are independent news outlets with no commercial or ownership tie to Cognition, McKinsey, Anthropic, or OpenAI -- well above the 2-of-4 minimum. Anthropic disclosure: required - missing (see disclosure finding above; filed as a clarification correction rather than blocking publication, since the lead's single comparative mention of Duet could plausibly be read as the policy's 'incidental... competing models' exemption, but the dedicated background paragraph and implications-section comparison tip the article into substantive treatment that the policy's disclosure rule is meant to cover).
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Central-tension claim verified: The Next Web's survey figures (334 leaders, top quarter more-than-doubled productivity, 30% saw productivity fall) are reported by The Next Web without any explanation of what distinguishes the two groups, and Fortune does not address the survey's internal split at all. The article's Implications section states this accurately ('Neither The Next Web nor Fortune reports what distinguishes the organizations in the top quarter from the 30% that saw declines') rather than inventing a reconciliation -- this is the correct, honest framing of an unresolved tension in the cited sources. All dates (Nov 16/17 2026 for Cognition's announcements, Sept 29 2026 for Dots, Oct 22 2026 for Duet, Oct 13 2026 for Citigroup's earnings call) match the source bylines/datelines. All specific figures (revenue run rate, valuation, financing talk, client counts, survey sample size) trace to the sources cited beside them. No orphan URLs: every URL in body_markdown appears in article.sources and vice versa. The cross-reference to the Herald's November 6 orchestration-layer Analysis was checked against the live article file (src/content/articles/2026-11/06-as-coding-agents-multiply-...md): the November 6 piece does carry a passing, unexamined Register reference to 'Claude Duet and Meta Muse' alongside Dots/Grok Bot and states 'The Herald has not independently examined those other products' -- the new submission accurately summarizes that passage and extends it with the Herald's own independent reporting on Duet and Dots, rather than re-narrating the November 6 article's content. Two quote-attribution errors found (see findings): 'frontier-level performance for 60% less' and 'even ship code' are each presented in quotation marks as if verbatim from the cited outlet, when in each case the outlet's own text is unquoted narration/paraphrase. The underlying facts both phrases convey are accurately sourced; only the quotation-mark treatment is wrong.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and analytical. Facts (Overview, Background, Current situation) are cleanly separated from analysis (Implications), as the Analysis format requires. The article is explicit about what the sources do and do not establish (e.g., 'Fortune does not report an independent test of these controls', 'the survey figures ... are not a measurement of Devin Bots or the McKinsey alliance itself'), which is good analytical discipline rather than overreach.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Herald coverage of Devin Bots or the Cognition-McKinsey alliance. Checked src/content/articles/2026-11/ for 'devin' and 'cognition' mentions: only the November 6 orchestration-layer Analysis mentions Cognition (for its November 2 hierarchical-budgets feature, a different, earlier event), and that article is correctly cited and built upon rather than duplicated.
concerns: Two body quotations ('frontier-level performance for 60% less' attributed to Cognition via The Next Web; 'even ship code' attributed to SiliconANGLE/Ahuja) are not verbatim text in their cited sources -- both are the outlet's own unquoted paraphrase/narration converted into a direct quotation. Neither is in the headline, summary, or lead; both are subordinate body claims where the underlying fact is accurately sourced.

Article names Anthropic in the lead and gives Claude Duet substantive, dedicated treatment in Background and Implications without including the one-sentence contributor-model-maker disclosure required by editorial policy.
recommendations: Future submissions: when an outlet describes what a company 'says' or 'claims' in the outlet's own sentence structure (no quotation marks in the source), do not add quotation marks around a fragment of that sentence in the Herald's rendering -- either drop the quote marks and keep it as reported paraphrase, or cite only phrases the source itself quotes.
Future submissions: include the Anthropic-maker disclosure sentence whenever an Anthropic product receives a dedicated paragraph of coverage, not only when Anthropic is the headline subject.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: This is a well-sourced, well-organized Analysis that meets the category's requirements (1536 words, 4 independent sources, facts separated from analysis, an examination of the McKinsey-survey tension rather than a release recap) and correctly builds on the Herald's prior November 6 reporting without re-narrating it. Two subordinate quote-attribution errors and a missing Anthropic disclosure sentence are the only issues found; none touch the headline, summary, or lead, and all three are honestly coverable in corrections records. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid analytical treatment of a notable but not industry-defining enterprise AI-coding development, useful to a developer/enterprise-tooling audience but not broadly transformative.
